questions.question: Which of the following government schemes focuses on the development of urban infrastructure in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AMRUT**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)** was launched in June 2015 by the Government of India to improve urban infrastructure.
 
• The mission focuses on **providing basic services** such as water supply, sewerage, urban transport, and green spaces to improve urban living standards.
 
• AMRUT follows a **decentralized approach**, empowering states and urban local bodies (ULBs) to plan and execute projects.
 
• The scheme aims to ensure **universal coverage of water supply and sewerage** services in all urban areas.
 
• Under AMRUT 2.0, launched in October 2021, the focus expanded to achieving **water sustainability** and promoting circular economy practices in urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smart Cities Mission**

 
 
• Launched in 2015, this mission focuses on creating **100 smart cities** across India by improving urban infrastructure and integrating technology.
 
• It aims at promoting sustainable and inclusive cities that provide core infrastructure and quality of life to its citizens.
 
• Key focus areas include smart mobility, smart governance, and smart energy.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U)**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, this scheme focuses on **providing affordable housing** to urban poor by 2022.
 
• It includes the **Credit-Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS)** for home loans and in-situ slum redevelopment projects.
 
• The scheme addresses housing shortages for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Low Income Groups (LIG), and Middle Income Groups (MIG).
 
 
 
• **RURBAN Mission**
 
 
• Also known as the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, it was launched in 2016 to **develop rural areas** by providing urban amenities.
 
• The mission aims to create **rurban clusters** by combining urban infrastructure with rural characteristics to promote balanced regional development.
 
 
 
• **MGNREGA**
 
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) focuses on providing **employment opportunities** in rural areas.
 
• It guarantees **100 days of wage employment** to rural households annually.

questions.question: Which of the following architectures was built by Aurangzeb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bibi-ka-Maqbara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bibi-ka-Maqbara** is a mausoleum located in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, and was built by Aurangzeb in memory of his first wife, Dilras Banu Begum.
 
• The construction of Bibi-ka-Maqbara began in 1651 and was completed in 1661 under the supervision of Aurangzeb's son, Azam Shah.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Taj of the Deccan" due to its resemblance to the Taj Mahal, although it is less grand in scale and detailing.
 
• The architecture was designed by Ata-ullah, the son of Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, who was the chief architect of the Taj Mahal.
 
• The structure is primarily made of marble and features intricate carvings, showcasing a blend of Mughal architectural styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurangzeb's Architectural Legacy:**

 
 
• Aurangzeb was not as prolific a patron of architecture as his predecessors; he focused more on military campaigns and administration.
 
• Bibi-ka-Maqbara is one of the few significant architectural projects commissioned during his reign.
 
• Unlike the Taj Mahal, Aurangzeb restricted excessive expenditure on monuments, reflecting his austere approach.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Mughal architecture is a blend of Islamic, Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles, characterized by domes, arches, minarets, and intricate ornamentation.
 
• Prominent examples include the Taj Mahal, Humayun’s Tomb, and Jama Masjid.
 
 
 
• **Other Monuments Built by Aurangzeb:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb built several mosques, such as the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore and the Moti Masjid in Delhi.
 
• These structures were more functional and less ornate compared to those built by earlier Mughal emperors.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Taj Mahal:**
 
 
• Bibi-ka-Maqbara’s resemblance to the Taj Mahal highlights the influence of Shah Jahan’s architectural style on Aurangzeb’s era.
 
• However, the materials used and the scale of construction were comparatively modest due to budgetary constraints imposed by Aurangzeb.

questions.question: Which category of musical instruments was related to objects of utility in daily life?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghana Vadya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ghana Vadya** refers to a category of musical instruments that produce sound through solid, non-stretched materials.
 
• These instruments are idiophones, meaning they generate sound by vibrating as a whole.
 
• Examples include cymbals, gongs, bells, and rattles, which were often derived from objects of utility in daily life.
 
• In traditional Indian music, Ghana Vadya instruments were used for rhythm and also served ceremonial and utilitarian purposes.
 
• The simplicity of these instruments made them accessible and integral to both folk and classical music traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Categories of Indian Musical Instruments:**

 
 
• **Ghana Vadya:** Idiophones producing sound by the vibration of the instrument itself.
 
• **Sushira Vadya:** Wind instruments like flutes and shehnai, producing sound through air vibration.
 
• **Tata Vadya:** String instruments like sitar and veena, where sound is produced by vibrating strings.
 
• **Avanaddh Vadya:** Percussion instruments with stretched membranes, like tabla and mridangam.
 
 
 
• **Idiophones:** A class of musical instruments where sound is produced by the material of the instrument itself without strings or membranes.
 
• **Utility in Daily Life:** Many Ghana Vadya instruments originated from tools or objects such as pots, bells, or metal plates, making them dual-purpose in nature.
 
• **Importance in Indian Tradition:** Instruments like manjira (cymbals) are used in devotional music and folk traditions, symbolizing rhythm and continuity.
 
• **Global Context:** Similar idiophones, like xylophones and maracas, are found in various cultures worldwide, showcasing the universality of Ghana Vadya-like instruments.

questions.question: How many poems are included in Behramji Merwanji Malabari’s 'The Indian Muse in English Garb'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Behramji Merwanji Malabari's **'The Indian Muse in English Garb'** is a collection of poems published in 1876.
 
• The book comprises a total of **32 poems**, showcasing the blending of Indian themes with English literary styles.
 
• Malabari was a notable Indian poet and social reformer, known for his advocacy against child marriage and for women's rights.
 
• The poems in the collection reflect themes of patriotism, spirituality, and social issues relevant to Indian society during the colonial era.
 
• This work exemplifies the cultural exchange between India and England during British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Behramji Malabari**:

 
 
• Born in 1853 in Baroda, Malabari was a prominent Indian poet, writer, and social reformer.
 
• He is best known for his efforts to abolish **child marriage** and improve the status of women in India.
 
• His writings combined progressive social ideas with literary creativity.
 
 
 
• **Indian Literature in English**:
 
 
• The late 19th century marked the rise of Indian authors writing in English, as part of cultural assimilation during British rule.
 
• Works such as 'The Indian Muse in English Garb' showcased Indian themes rendered in English literary tradition.
 
• This genre helped bridge cultural gaps and introduced Indian perspectives to Western audiences.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Influence on Indian Writing**:
 
 
• During British rule, Indian writers adopted English as a medium to express social, political, and cultural narratives.
 
• It led to the evolution of Indo-Anglian literature, which remains a significant part of Indian literary heritage.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform in 19th Century India**:
 
 
• The period saw the emergence of reformers like Malabari, who sought to address issues such as child marriage, widow remarriage, and women's education.
 
• Literature often served as a vehicle for promoting these reformist ideas.

questions.question: Morarji Desai was commemorated on his 129th birth anniversary, 28 February 2025, for his contributions to governance reforms in India. Which of the following commissions did he chair in 1966 to restructure the country’s governance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1st Administrative Reforms Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **1st Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC)** was established in 1966 under the chairmanship of **Morarji Desai** to review and recommend changes to the administrative structure of India.
 
• The Commission submitted its reports over the next few years, covering various aspects of administration such as personnel management, financial administration, and center-state relations.
 
• It focused on **reforms in governance** to make the Indian administrative system more efficient, transparent, and responsive to the needs of citizens.
 
• The 1st ARC produced **20 detailed reports**, which included over 500 actionable recommendations.
 
• Some of the key areas addressed included **administrative accountability, ethics in governance, and citizen-centric services.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC)**:

 
 
• The ARC is constituted by the government to examine the state of public administration and suggest reforms.
 
• The recommendations of the 1st ARC laid the foundation for modern governance reforms in India.
 
• Its reports covered areas such as local governance, interdepartmental coordination, and the role of public sector enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Morarji Desai**:
 
 
• He was the 4th Prime Minister of India and served from 1977 to 1979.
 
• Desai was known for his integrity, administrative skills, and commitment to governance reforms.
 
• He played a vital role in shaping India's administrative policies during his tenure as a public servant and leader.
 
 
 
• **Key Impact of the 1st ARC**:
 
 
• The reports influenced the creation of institutions such as the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) and reforms in personnel management.
 
• It emphasized the importance of ethics, accountability, and citizen participation in governance.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent ARCs**:
 
 
• The 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission (2005-2009) built upon the recommendations of the 1st ARC.
 
• It focused on improving governance in areas such as disaster management, e-governance, and local self-governance.

questions.question: Desert soil is mostly found in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Desert soil** is predominantly found in Rajasthan, which houses the majority of the **Thar Desert**, also known as the Great Indian Desert.
 
• Rajasthan's desert soil is characterized by **low organic matter, sandy texture, and poor water retention capacity**.
 
• Such soil is typically formed due to **arid climatic conditions** and lacks sufficient vegetation cover.
 
• The **western parts of Rajasthan**, including districts like Jaisalmer, Barmer, and Bikaner, are most affected by desertification and have extensive coverage of desert soil.
 
• Desert soil is primarily used for growing drought-resistant crops like **millets, pulses, and mustard**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• Located in northwest India, the Thar Desert is the world's 17th largest desert and covers about **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• It spans across Rajasthan and extends into parts of Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana.
 
• The Thar Desert plays a crucial role in shaping the soil composition of western Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Desertification:**
 
 
• Desertification refers to the process by which fertile land becomes desert, typically due to **drought, deforestation, or inappropriate agricultural practices**.
 
• Rajasthan is one of the Indian states most affected by desertification.
 
• Government initiatives like the **Desert Development Programme** aim to counter desertification in the region.
 
 
 
• **Soil Composition in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• In addition to desert soil, Rajasthan also has **alluvial soil** in regions near rivers like Chambal and **black soil** in parts of the southeastern region.
 
• Desert soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, which are critical for high agricultural yield.
 
 
 
• **Climate of Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Rajasthan has a predominantly **arid and semi-arid climate**, with temperatures ranging from extreme heat in summers to extreme cold in winters.
 
• Annual rainfall in desert regions of Rajasthan is generally **less than 150 mm**, contributing to the formation of desert soil.

questions.question: What natural feature existed between the Himalayas and the Deccan Plateau before the formation of the Great Plain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A shallow trough or geosyncline**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indo-Gangetic Plain, also called the Great Plain, was formed due to the gradual filling of a **shallow trough or geosyncline** that existed between the Himalayas and the Deccan Plateau.
 
• This geosyncline, known as the **Tethys Sea**, was a depression that existed millions of years ago during the Mesozoic era.
 
• Over time, sediments from the rising Himalayas and other sources filled this trough, leading to the formation of the vast alluvial plains of Northern India.
 
• The process of sedimentation was facilitated by rivers like the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra, which transported eroded material from the mountains to the plains.
 
• The Great Plain is now one of the most fertile regions in the world, supporting agriculture and a dense population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geosyncline:**

 
 
• A geosyncline is a large-scale depression in the Earth's crust filled with thick layers of sediments.
 
• It often forms in areas where two tectonic plates converge, leading to subsidence and sediment accumulation.
 
• Over geological time, geosynclines may become mountain ranges or plains due to tectonic uplift and erosion.
 
 
 
• **Tethys Sea:**
 
 
• The Tethys Sea was a prehistoric ocean that existed between the ancient continents of Laurasia (to the north) and Gondwana (to the south).
 
• It played a key role in the tectonic evolution of Asia, Europe, and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Its closure due to the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate led to the uplift of the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Sedimentation:**
 
 
• The Himalayas are the primary source of sediments that filled the Indo-Gangetic trough.
 
• Rivers originating from the Himalayas carry eroded materials and deposit them in the plains.
 
• This sedimentation process has been ongoing for millions of years, shaping the fertile plains.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Gangetic Plain:**
 
 
• One of the world's largest alluvial plains, extending over 7 lakh square kilometers across India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.
 
• It is drained by major rivers, including the Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries.
 
• The plain is known for its rich soil, which supports intensive agriculture and sustains a high population density.

questions.question: If it is 12 noon at IST (82°30′E), what time is it approximately at 97°30′E longitude?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1:00 PM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on the longitude of 82º30′E, which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT (Greenwich Mean Time).
 
• Each degree of longitude corresponds to a time difference of 4 minutes. Moving eastward adds time, while moving westward subtracts time.
 
• The difference in longitude between 82º30′E (IST) and 97º30′E is 15 degrees.
 
• 15 degrees corresponds to a time difference of 15 × 4 = 60 minutes (1 hour).
 
• Therefore, if it is 12 noon at 82º30′E (IST), the time at 97º30′E will be 1:00 PM.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Longitude and Time Relationship**

 
 
• The Earth is divided into 360 degrees of longitude, and the rotation of the Earth takes 24 hours, meaning 15 degrees per hour.
 
• Each degree of longitude represents a time difference of 4 minutes (60 minutes ÷ 15 degrees).
 
 
 
• **Standard Meridian**
 
 
• Standard time is calculated based on a specific longitude called the standard meridian of a region.
 
• India’s standard meridian is 82º30′E, which passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Time Zones**
 
 
• Time zones are regions on Earth with the same standard time, usually spaced at 15-degree intervals of longitude.
 
• Countries like India use a single time zone for the entire country, while others like the USA use multiple time zones.
 
 
 
• **Eastward vs Westward Time Calculation**
 
 
• When moving eastward, time is added to the standard time of the reference meridian.
 
• When moving westward, time is subtracted from the standard time of the reference meridian.

questions.question: Who among the following issued the earliest land grant of the Maitraka family in 502 CE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dronasimha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dronasimha** was a ruler of the Maitraka dynasty, which was established in the early 6th century CE in Gujarat.
 
• The earliest land grant by the Maitraka family, dated to **502 CE**, was issued by Dronasimha.
 
• The Maitrakas were known for their patronage of Brahmanical Hinduism and grant practices to promote religious and social welfare.
 
• Dronasimha’s rule marked the beginning of the Maitraka dynasty, which rose to prominence in Western India.
 
• The Maitraka rulers, including Dronasimha, were instrumental in the development of administrative systems and religious institutions in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maitraka Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Maitraka dynasty was established in Gujarat, India, in the early 6th century CE.
 
• The dynasty is believed to have been founded by a military officer who declared independence from the Gupta Empire.
 
• Its capital was located at Vallabhi, which became a center of learning and culture during their reign.
 
 
 
• **Land Grants in Ancient India:**
 
 
• Land grants were commonly issued by rulers to Brahmins, temples, or monasteries for religious and social purposes.
 
• These grants often came with tax exemptions and administrative privileges.
 
• They were recorded on copper plates, which served as official documents of the grant.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Copper Plates:**
 
 
• Copper plates were used in ancient India to record significant events such as land grants and royal decrees.
 
• They provide valuable historical evidence about administrative practices, religion, and society.
 
• Many copper plates from the Maitraka dynasty have been discovered, offering insights into their governance and culture.
 
 
 
• **Vallabhi as a Learning Center:**
 
 
• Under the Maitraka dynasty, Vallabhi became an important center for Buddhist and Brahmanical learning.
 
• Scholars from Vallabhi contributed significantly to literature, philosophy, and religious discourse.
 
• The Maitraka rulers supported educational and cultural activities, enhancing the region's intellectual legacy.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms was performed by 'Maharis' as part of temple service?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Odissi** is a classical Indian dance form that originated in **Odisha**.
 
• It is one of the **oldest dance forms in India**, with its roots tracing back to **200 BCE.**
 
• The dance was historically performed by **Maharis**, who were **female temple dancers**, as part of their service to Lord **Jagannath** in Odisha.
 
• Maharis dedicated their performances to **spiritual devotion**, portraying mythological stories and religious themes.
 
• **Odissi** is characterized by intricate movements, **graceful postures,** and expressions known as **Bhaav.**
 
• The dance style also incorporates elements of **Natya** (drama), **Nritta** (pure dance), and **Nritya** (expressive dance).
 
• Today, **Odissi** is performed globally and remains a significant part of India's cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kathak**__

 __
 
• **Kathak** originated in northern India and is based on storytelling, derived from the Sanskrit word **Katha**, meaning "story."
 
• This dance form incorporates intricate **footwork**, spins, and emotive expressions known as **Abhinaya.**
 
• Kathak has three main gharanas: **Lucknow, Jaipur,** and **Banaras.**
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**__
 __
 
• **Kathakali** originated in **Kerala** and is a highly stylized classical dance-drama.
 
• It is known for its elaborate costumes, **facial makeup,** and intricate hand gestures or **Mudras.**
 
• Kathakali is typically performed during **night-long events** depicting stories from **Indian epics** like the **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana.**
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**__
 
 
• **Kuchipudi** originated in **Andhra Pradesh** and is characterized by its **fluid movements** and dramatic storytelling.
 
• This dance form combines elements of **speech, music, and acting** with dance.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often include a blend of solo and group dances.

questions.question: Commemorated on National Science Day, CV Raman established key scientific platforms in India. The scientific journal founded by him was _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Journal of Physics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Journal of Physics** was founded by **CV Raman** in the year **1926**.
 
• This journal holds a significant place in the history of Indian science and research as it provided a platform for scientists to publish their work during the early 20th century.
 
• CV Raman, a Nobel Laureate in Physics (1930), established this journal to encourage and promote scientific research in India.
 
• It is one of the oldest scientific journals in India and continues to be published to this day.
 
• The focus of the journal is on publishing high-quality research in the field of **physics**, covering a wide range of topics such as **optics, quantum mechanics, condensed matter physics, and more.**
 
• The journal played a pivotal role in advancing the scientific community in India and fostering collaborations with international researchers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Current Science**__

 __
 
• The **Current Science** journal is a multidisciplinary science journal published in India.
 
• It was first published in **1932**, and its primary focus is to disseminate important research in various scientific disciplines.
 
• Although it is another key Indian scientific publication, it was not founded by **CV Raman** but is associated with the **Indian Academy of Sciences.**
 
 
 
• **Nature India**__
 __
 
• **Nature India** is a localized version of the internationally renowned **Nature journal**.
 
• It focuses on highlighting high-quality research and scientific advancements emerging from **India.**
 
• This publication is a part of the **Springer Nature group** and was not founded by CV Raman.
 
 
 
• **Science India Monthly**__
 
 
• The **Science India Monthly** is a popular science magazine aimed at spreading awareness about scientific developments in India.
 
• This publication focuses on making science accessible to a broader audience, including students and enthusiasts.
 
• It is not associated with CV Raman.

questions.question: The Lipulekh Pass, important for India’s border trade, lies between India and ___________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tibet (China)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lipulekh Pass** is a strategic mountain pass located in the Himalayas.
 
• It lies at the **tri-junction of India, Nepal, and China (Tibet).**
 
• The pass has historically been used for **pilgrimage routes**, including the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.
 
• It serves as an important point for **border trade** between India and Tibet (China).
 
• In recent years, the area has been a subject of **geopolitical discussions** due to its strategic significance.
 
• The Lipulekh Pass is located in the **Pithoragarh district** of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It is situated at an elevation of approximately **5,200 meters above sea level.**
 
• The pass has a historical significance as it was mentioned in treaties like the **1815 Treaty of Sugauli.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bangladesh**__

 __
 
• Bangladesh shares a border with India but does not have mountain passes like Lipulekh as its terrain is mostly **plains and delta regions.**
 
• It is located to the **east of India** and is separated by the **Radcliffe Line.**
 
• The country is known for rivers like the **Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna.**
 
 
 
• **Bhutan**__
 __
 
• Bhutan is a landlocked country sharing a border with India but does not have the **Lipulekh Pass.**
 
• It lies to the northeast of India and is known for the **Himalayan mountain range.**
 
• The country has close ties with India under the **Indo-Bhutan Friendship Treaty.**
 
 
 
• **Afghanistan**__
 
 
• Afghanistan shares no common border with India and is separated by **Pakistan.**
 
• The terrain of Afghanistan primarily includes **mountains and arid regions.**
 
• India engages with Afghanistan through development projects and historical ties, but it does not involve any direct mountain passes like Lipulekh.

questions.question: In which year was 'Make in India' launched by the Government of India to facilitate investment, foster innovation, enhance skill development, protect intellectual property, and build best in class manufacturing infrastructure in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **‘Make in India’ initiative** was launched by the Government of India on **25th September 2014**.
 
• The program was aimed at transforming India into a global **manufacturing hub**.
 
• It focuses on **enhancing skill development, fostering innovation**, and **protecting intellectual property**.
 
• The initiative encourages both **domestic and foreign companies** to manufacture their products in India.
 
• The program is managed by the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)** under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• ‘Make in India’ emphasizes key sectors such as **automobiles, chemicals, IT, pharmaceuticals, textiles, defense manufacturing, and food processing**, among others.
 
• The initiative aims to improve the **ease of doing business** and strengthen India's position in the **global supply chain**.
 
• India's ranking in the **World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Index** has significantly improved since the launch of this program.
 
• The ‘Make in India’ initiative aligns with the broader vision of achieving a **$5 trillion economy** by 2025.

questions.question: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), a flagship mission aimed at addressing the urban housing shortage in India, launched?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2015**__.

• The scheme also promotes the use of **sustainable and eco-friendly construction technologies.**
 
• PMAY supports the vision of the **Housing for All** initiative, aligning with the goals of inclusive growth and urban development.

questions.question: Gaddi Nati is the famous folk dance of which of the following States?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gaddi Nati** is a **traditional folk dance** of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• This dance form is predominantly performed by the **Gaddi tribe**, which is a nomadic tribal community residing in the **Kangra, Chamba, and Kullu districts** of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• Gaddi Nati is performed during **festivals, fairs, and social gatherings**.
 
• The dance is characterized by its **graceful movements**, often depicting **stories of mythology, daily life, and cultural traditions**.
 
• The performers usually wear **traditional attire**, including **embroidered woolen garments** and headgear, reflecting the local culture and climate.
 
• It is accompanied by **folk music** played on instruments such as the **dhol, nagara, and flute**.
 
• In 2015, **Gaddi Nati** was recognized as one of the **longest folk dances** to be performed in a single stretch, showcasing its cultural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh**__

 __
 
• Madhya Pradesh is known for its rich cultural heritage and folk dances such as **Tertali, Jawara, and Matki**, but it is not associated with the Gaddi Nati dance.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh**__
 __
 
• Uttar Pradesh is famous for its folk dances like **Ras Leela and Charkula**, which are rooted in the region's connection to the life of **Lord Krishna**.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__
 
 
• Andhra Pradesh features traditional dances such as **Kuchipudi** (a classical dance form) and folk dances like **Veeranatyam**, but it has no relation to Gaddi Nati.

questions.question: Which of the following novels, published in 1961, was written by Attia Hosain and portrays the impact of the Partition on a feudal family?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sunlight on the Broken Column**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sunlight on the Broken Column** is a novel written by **Attia Hosain**, published in the year **1961**.
 
• The novel is set in the background of the **Partition of India**, which divided British India into two countries: India and Pakistan.
 
• It portrays the **impact of Partition** on a **feudal family** and explores themes of tradition, change, and personal identity.
 
• The protagonist, Laila, navigates her life amidst the **upheaval of Partition**, addressing issues such as **patriarchy, familial expectations**, and **political turmoil**.
 
• The novel is significant for its vivid depiction of the **social and cultural transformation** that accompanied the historical event of Partition.
 
• **Attia Hosain**, the author, was also a noted writer, broadcaster, and journalist, who brought a unique perspective to her writing as a member of the Muslim aristocracy in pre-Partition India.
 
• The novel is considered a **classic piece of literature** that offers an insightful portrayal of the socio-political challenges during a critical period in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Clear Light of Day**__

 __
 
• Written by **Anita Desai**, this novel was published in **1980**.
 
• It focuses on the dynamics of a middle-class family in Old Delhi and explores themes such as **family relationships, memory, and time.**
 
• Unlike "Sunlight on the Broken Column," it does not directly deal with the Partition.
 
 
 
• **Ice Candy Man**__
 __
 
• Written by **Bapsi Sidhwa**, this novel is also known as **Cracking India**.
 
• It depicts the Partition of India through the eyes of a young girl, Lenny, in Lahore.
 
• The novel is notable for its portrayal of communal violence and the human impact of Partition.
 
 
 
• **Midnight’s Children**__
 
 
• Written by **Salman Rushdie**, this iconic novel was published in **1981**.
 
• The book blends **magical realism** with historical fiction, narrating the story of India’s transition from British colonialism to independence and Partition.
 
• It is a celebrated work but is distinct in style and narrative from Attia Hosain's novel.

questions.question: In Warli painting, what is the process called where cow dung and water are spread for background preparation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lipane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Warli painting** is a traditional tribal art form practiced by the Warli tribe of Maharashtra, India.
 
• The process of spreading a mixture of cow dung and water to prepare the background is called **Lipane**.
 
• **Lipane** creates a dark, natural, and textured surface for painting, which contrasts beautifully with the white rice paste used for the artwork.
 
• Traditionally, the walls of huts were prepared with Lipane before adorning them with symbolic and intricate Warli patterns.
 
• This technique reflects the tribe's connection with nature and their sustainable art practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Warli Art**:

 
 
• Warli painting is a tribal art form that dates back to around 2500 BCE.
 
• It uses simple geometric shapes like circles, triangles, and lines to depict scenes from daily life, folklore, and nature.
 
• The paintings are monochromatic, using white pigment made from rice paste and natural gum on a mud-brown background.
 
 
 
• **Symbolism in Warli Art**:
 
 
• Warli art is deeply symbolic, often depicting themes of harmony between humans and nature.
 
• Common motifs include farming activities, festivals, wildlife, and community rituals.
 
 
 
• **Eco-Friendly Practices**:
 
 
• The materials used in Warli art—such as rice paste, cow dung, and mud—are completely natural and biodegradable.
 
• This reflects the tribe's eco-conscious lifestyle and their reverence for the environment.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts**:
 
 
• Warli art has gained international recognition and is being preserved as an important cultural heritage.
 
• Government bodies and NGOs are working to promote the art form and improve the livelihood of Warli artists.

questions.question: Which of the following reformers was NOT associated with British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aryabhatta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aryabhatta** was a renowned Indian mathematician and astronomer who lived during the Gupta period, around the 5th-6th century CE.
 
• He is primarily associated with ancient India, predating the British colonial period by many centuries.
 
• Aryabhatta's contributions include the approximation of pi (π) and the introduction of the concept of zero in mathematics.
 
• Unlike Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Swami Vivekananda, Aryabhatta was not involved in socio-religious or political reform movements in British India.
 
• His works, such as the "Aryabhatiya," focused on mathematics, astronomy, and science rather than social or political reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**

 
 
• Known as the "Father of Modern India," he was a prominent socio-religious reformer of the 19th century.
 
• He founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 to combat social evils like sati and promote education and women's rights.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the abolition of the practice of sati in British India.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**
 
 
• A nationalist leader and freedom fighter, Tilak was one of the prominent leaders of the Indian independence movement.
 
• He is often referred to as "Lokmanya" and is known for the famous slogan "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it."
 
• Tilak contributed significantly to the Swadeshi Movement and initiated Ganesh Chaturthi as a public celebration to unite Indians.
 
 
 
• **Swami Vivekananda**
 
 
• A Hindu monk and social reformer, Swami Vivekananda is best known for his speech at the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893.
 
• He was a disciple of Ramakrishna Paramhansa and founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.
 
• His teachings emphasized youth empowerment, spirituality, and service to society.
 
 
 
• **Aryabhatta's Legacy**
 
 
• His work, "Aryabhatiya," is divided into four sections and covers topics like arithmetic, algebra, trigonometry, and astronomy.
 
• He proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system and explained the rotation of Earth around its axis.
 
• Aryabhatta's contributions laid the foundation for later advancements in mathematics and astronomy in India and beyond.

questions.question: Which of the following is the war dance of the Nagas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rangma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rangma** is a traditional war dance performed by the Naga tribes of Nagaland, symbolizing bravery and martial prowess.
 
• This dance is performed during ceremonies and festivals, particularly to commemorate victories in battles or to invoke courage.
 
• The dancers often wear traditional warrior attire, including headgear adorned with feathers and ornaments representing tribal identity.
 
• The dance movements mimic combat actions, showcasing the agility and fighting skills of the performers.
 
• Rangma dance is an integral part of the Naga culture, reflecting the community's strong warrior tradition and historical significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Naga Tribes:**

 
 
• The Nagas are a group of indigenous tribes residing primarily in Nagaland, northeastern India, as well as parts of Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, and Myanmar.
 
• Each Naga tribe has its unique customs, traditions, and dialects, making their culture highly diverse.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Dances of Nagaland:**
 
 
• Other dances include the Sumi war dance, performed during festivals like Tuluni and Ahuna.
 
• These dances often serve as expressions of gratitude, celebration, and community bonding.
 
 
 
• **Festivals of Nagaland:**
 
 
• Hornbill Festival is the most prominent festival, showcasing the diverse cultural heritage of all Naga tribes.
 
• It is held annually in December and features traditional dances, music, arts, and crafts.
 
 
 
• **Significance of War Dances:**
 
 
• War dances in tribal communities often represent valor, unity, and preparation for battle.
 
• They also serve as a medium to pass down ancestral stories and warrior skills to younger generations.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the Imperial Service Scheme (1885)?

options.text: To raise troops for British defence, paid by princely states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To raise troops for British defence, paid by princely states**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Imperial Service Scheme was introduced in **1885** during British colonial rule in India.
 
• The scheme aimed at raising **military forces** from Indian princely states to support the British Empire’s defense.
 
• Under this scheme, troops were recruited, trained, and maintained by princely states but were available for use by the British government in times of need.
 
• It provided princely states with an opportunity to demonstrate loyalty to the British Crown by contributing militarily.
 
• These troops were often deployed in various military campaigns beyond India, including in British imperial conflicts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Princely States:**

 
 
• During British rule, India was divided into British-controlled territories and approximately 565 princely states governed by local rulers under British suzerainty.
 
• Princely states retained internal autonomy but pledged allegiance to the British Crown.
 
 
 
• **British Imperial Defense:**
 
 
• Defense was a critical concern for the British Empire, particularly during global conflicts like World War I and II.
 
• Indian troops, including those raised under schemes like the Imperial Service Scheme, played significant roles in British military campaigns worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Role of Indian Troops in the British Army:**
 
 
• Indian soldiers served in various capacities, including infantry, cavalry, and specialized units, under British command.
 
• Their participation in imperial wars earned them recognition but also highlighted the exploitative nature of colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Princely States:**
 
 
• While contributing troops enhanced the prestige of princely rulers, it also placed financial burdens on the states to maintain military forces.
 
• It created a closer dependency on British support and control.

questions.question: Which region was merged in 1948 to form the initial territory of Himachal Pradesh?

options.text: Patiala and East Punjab States Union

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shimla Hill States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Himachal Pradesh was initially formed on 15 April 1948 by merging 30 princely states known as **Shimla Hill States**.
 
• These states included prominent regions such as Chamba, Mandi, Suket, Baghal, and Bhagat, among others.
 
• The merger was part of India's post-independence reorganization of states to streamline administration and governance.
 
• The Shimla Hill States were small princely states located primarily in the hilly areas of Punjab Province during British India.
 
• The formation of Himachal Pradesh laid the foundation for its eventual recognition as a full-fledged state in 1971.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formation of Himachal Pradesh:**

 
 
• On 15 April 1948, Himachal Pradesh was created as a Chief Commissioner's Province by merging 30 princely states.
 
• It was made a Union Territory on 1 November 1956, and became a full-fledged state on 25 January 1971.
 
 
 
• **Shimla Hill States:**
 
 
• These were princely states in the hilly regions of Punjab Province during British India.
 
• They were governed by local rulers under the suzerainty of the British Empire.
 
 
 
• **State Reorganization Post-Independence:**
 
 
• India's independence in 1947 led to the integration of princely states into larger administrative units.
 
• Many smaller states were merged to create streamlined governance structures.
 
 
 
• **Current Significance:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is known for its scenic beauty, cultural heritage, and as a prominent tourist destination.
 
• The state contributes significantly to India's agriculture, hydropower, and tourism sectors.

questions.question:
Which of the following banking facilities is/are operated by National Payments Corporation of India?

1. National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT)

2. Aadhaar Enabled Payment System

3. UPI Lite
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)** operates innovative payment systems and solutions in India.
 
• **Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS):** Allows basic banking services using Aadhaar authentication.
 
• **UPI Lite:** A simplified version of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for small-value offline transactions.
 
• NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer) is operated by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, not NPCI.
 
• NPCI focuses on digital payment systems like UPI, AePS, RuPay, and IMPS to enhance financial inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI):**

 
 
• Established in 2008 under the guidance of the RBI and Indian Banks' Association (IBA).
 
• Key initiatives include UPI, RuPay, IMPS, BHIM, and AePS.
 
• Aims to create robust payment infrastructure and promote digital payments in India.
 
 
 
• **Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS):**
 
 
• Facilitates cash withdrawal, balance inquiry, and fund transfer using Aadhaar authentication.
 
• Promotes financial inclusion by enabling banking services in rural and remote areas.
 
 
 
• **Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and UPI Lite:**
 
 
• UPI enables instant fund transfers between bank accounts using mobile devices.
 
• UPI Lite is designed for low-value transactions, especially in offline scenarios.
 
 
 
• **National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT):**
 
 
• An electronic payment system for transferring funds between banks in India.
 
• Operated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to facilitate secure and reliable fund transfers.

questions.question: In Carnatic music, the concluding part of 'Pallavi' is usually known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ragamalika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Carnatic music, **Ragamalika** refers to a composition in which multiple ragas are used sequentially.
 
• The concluding part of the Pallavi, often called "Ragamalika," showcases **the artist's creativity and mastery** of various ragas.
 
• Ragamalika is typically performed in the **final segment of a Pallavi** during a concert, adding variety and vibrancy to the performance.
 
• This segment often involves transitions between ragas, requiring **technical precision and aesthetic understanding**.
 
• Ragamalika compositions are highly regarded for their **melodic richness and lyrical beauty**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pallavi:**

 
 
• The Pallavi is the first section of a Carnatic music composition and serves as the thematic base.
 
• It is known for its **structured melody and rhythm**, setting the tone for improvisation.
 
• The Pallavi often highlights the raga and tala chosen for the composition.
 
 
 
• **Anu Pallavi:**
 
 
• The Anu Pallavi follows the Pallavi and acts as a bridge to the next section.
 
• It is typically shorter but complements the Pallavi in terms of melody and rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Thanam:**
 
 
• Thanam refers to rhythmic improvisation in a raga, often performed during Ragam Thanam Pallavi.
 
• It showcases the artist's mastery over rhythm and melody.
 
 
 
• **Ragamalika Compositions:**
 
 
• Ragamalika compositions are a unique feature of Carnatic music, blending multiple ragas into a single piece.
 
• Famous composers like **Muthuswami Dikshitar** and **Tyagaraja** have contributed to Ragamalika compositions.

questions.question: Which novel by Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie portrays the interconnected lives of four African women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Half of a Yellow Sun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Half of a Yellow Sun** is a novel written by Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, published in 2006.
 
• The book portrays the lives of four central characters during the Nigerian Civil War (1967–1970), also known as the Biafran War.
 
• The narrative focuses on the interconnected lives of Ugwu (a houseboy), Olanna (a professor), Richard (a British expatriate), and Kainene (Olanna's twin sister).
 
• The title of the novel refers to the flag of Biafra, which features a half sun, symbolizing the struggle for independence during the war.
 
• It won the **Orange Prize for Fiction** in 2007 and is considered a landmark work in African literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie**

 
 
• An acclaimed Nigerian author known for her works exploring themes of identity, feminism, and post-colonialism.
 
• Other notable works include *Purple Hibiscus*, *Americanah*, and her essay *We Should All Be Feminists*.
 
 
 
• **Nigerian Civil War**
 
 
• Also referred to as the Biafran War, it was a conflict from 1967 to 1970 between Nigeria and the Republic of Biafra, which sought independence.
 
• The war resulted in significant casualties, with famine and humanitarian crises affecting millions.
 
 
 
• **Orange Prize for Fiction**
 
 
• Now known as the Women’s Prize for Fiction, it is an annual award celebrating excellence in women’s writing worldwide.
 
• Adichie won this prestigious award for *Half of a Yellow Sun* in 2007.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Novel**
 
 
• *Half of a Yellow Sun* brought global attention to the Nigerian Civil War and its aftermath.
 
• The novel has been adapted into a film, released in 2013, starring Thandie Newton and Chiwetel Ejiofor.

questions.question: The Northern Plains of India have been primarily formed by which of the following processes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deposition of alluvium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Northern Plains of India were formed due to the **deposition of alluvial soil brought by the rivers** originating from the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• The plains are composed of layers of **fine silt, sand, and clay** deposited over millions of years.
 
• The three major Himalayan rivers—**the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Indus**—along with their tributaries, played a crucial role in shaping these fertile plains.
 
• This region is known for its **fertile soil**, making it one of the most agriculturally productive areas in India.
 
• The Northern Plains are categorized into three sections—**the Bhabar, the Terai, and the Alluvial Plains** (Khadar and Bangar).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvium:**

 
 
• Alluvium refers to the **fine-grained fertile soil** deposited by rivers over time.
 
• This type of soil is rich in minerals and nutrients, making it suitable for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Rivers:**
 
 
• The rivers originating from the Himalayas, such as the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus, are **perennial**, meaning they flow throughout the year.
 
• These rivers are fed by **glacial melt** and monsoon rains.
 
 
 
• **Bhabar and Terai:**
 
 
• **Bhabar:** A narrow belt of coarse gravel and pebbles found at the foothills of the Himalayas.
 
• **Terai:** A marshy and swampy region south of the Bhabar, characterized by dense vegetation.
 
 
 
• **Khadar and Bangar:**
 
 
• **Khadar:** The newer, fertile alluvial soil found in the river's floodplains.
 
• **Bangar:** The older alluvial soil found further away from the riverbanks, less fertile than Khadar.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Significance:**
 
 
• The Northern Plains are often referred to as the "Granary of India" due to their high agricultural output.
 
• Main crops grown in the region include wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.

questions.question: Skill development became crucial in aligning the workforce with economic needs. Which flagship program was launched in 2015 to improve employability through skill training?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Skill India Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Skill India Mission** was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on **15 July 2015**.
 
• This flagship program aims to **train over 40 crore people in India** in various skills by 2022.
 
• It focuses on enhancing employability by providing **industry-relevant skill training** to the youth.
 
• The initiative encompasses a range of schemes such as **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)**, National Skill Development Mission, and Skill Loan Scheme.
 
• The program emphasizes creating a skilled workforce aligned with **market demand and economic needs**, fostering entrepreneurship and job creation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)**

 
 
• PMKVY is a key component of Skill India Mission and was launched in 2015.
 
• It provides **short-term skill development training** and certification to boost employability.
 
• Focuses on sectors with high growth potential identified by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).
 
• Offers monetary rewards to trainees post-certification to encourage participation.
 
 
 
• **National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)**
 
 
• NSDC is a public-private partnership organization established in 2009 under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
 
• Its goal is to promote skill development by catalyzing the creation of large, quality vocational training institutions.
 
• It supports private sector initiatives in skill development through funding and capacity building.
 
 
 
• **Skill Loan Scheme**
 
 
• Launched under Skill India Mission, it provides loans ranging from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 1.5 lakh for skill training programs.
 
• The scheme aims to make skill development affordable and accessible to the youth.
 
• Loan repayment begins one year after the completion of the course.
 
 
 
• **National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF)**
 
 
• NSQF is a competency-based framework that organizes qualifications based on levels of knowledge, skills, and aptitude.
 
• It aims to standardize and integrate skill development programs across various sectors.
 
• The framework facilitates mobility between vocational and academic streams.

questions.question: Financial inclusion has been a major goal of post-1991 economic reforms in India. Which of the following flagship schemes was launched in 2014 to promote financial inclusion through universal access to banking facilities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on **28th August 2014** to promote financial inclusion in India.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **universal access to banking services**, including savings accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension.
 
• Under PMJDY, individuals can open a **zero-balance savings account** with access to a RuPay debit card and accidental insurance cover.
 
• The scheme is an integral part of India's financial inclusion strategy and has resulted in the opening of millions of bank accounts, particularly in rural areas.
 
• PMJDY includes additional benefits such as **overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000** for account holders and direct benefit transfer (DBT) integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Inclusion**

 
 
• It refers to the process of ensuring access to financial services and adequate credit at affordable costs for all individuals, especially the marginalized and low-income groups.
 
• Financial inclusion helps reduce poverty by enabling people to save, borrow, and invest.
 
 
 
• **RuPay Debit Card**
 
 
• RuPay is India's indigenous payment network developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
 
• PMJDY account holders are provided with RuPay debit cards that offer accidental insurance cover.
 
 
 
• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**
 
 
• DBT ensures that subsidies and benefits are directly transferred to the bank accounts of beneficiaries.
 
• This reduces leakages and ensures transparency in government schemes.
 
 
 
• **Impact of PMJDY**
 
 
• As of 2023, PMJDY has helped open over 48 crore bank accounts, with a significant proportion in rural areas.
 
• The scheme has facilitated access to formal banking services for millions of previously unbanked individuals.

questions.question: The folk song of Kerala, which is sung to send away the evil ghosts and spirits, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhuta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhuta** is a traditional folk song of Kerala that is sung to ward off evil spirits and ghosts.
 
• The term "Bhuta" translates to "spirit" or "ghost" in several Dravidian languages, including Malayalam.
 
• This folk art is deeply rooted in the cultural and spiritual practices of Kerala, especially in rural areas.
 
• Bhuta songs are often performed during ceremonies or rituals aimed at exorcism or invoking protective deities.
 
• The practice is tied to the belief in animism, which attributes spiritual significance to natural elements and entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Folklore of Kerala:**

 
 
• Kerala has a rich tradition of folk arts, including songs, dances, and rituals, that reflect its cultural diversity.
 
• Other significant folk traditions of Kerala include Theyyam, Padayani, and Ottamthullal.
 
• These traditions are often performed during festivals and religious ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Animism in Indian Culture:**
 
 
• Animism is the belief that spirits or supernatural forces inhabit natural objects and phenomena.
 
• This belief is prevalent in many tribal and rural communities in India, including Kerala.
 
• Rituals and songs like Bhuta are part of animistic practices aimed at maintaining harmony with these forces.
 
 
 
• **Ceremonial Contexts:**
 
 
• Bhuta songs are typically performed during specific ceremonies, including housewarming, temple festivals, and exorcisms.
 
• They are accompanied by traditional musical instruments like drums and cymbals.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Linguistic Identity:**
 
 
• Malayalam is the official language of Kerala and is one of the 22 scheduled languages of India.
 
• Many folk traditions, including Bhuta songs, are preserved in the Malayalam language.

questions.question: The famous dance form 'Kuchipudi' derives its name from the village Kuchelapuram, which is located in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and originates from **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The dance form derives its name from the village **Kuchelapuram**, also known as Kuchipudi, located in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi combines **dance, acting, and narration**, making it a dance-drama tradition.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in **Natya Shastra**, an ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts.
 
• Kuchipudi performances traditionally begin with a prayer and are accompanied by Carnatic music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natya Shastra**

 
 
• An ancient Indian treatise on performing arts written by **Bharata Muni**.
 
• It outlines the principles of classical dance, drama, and music.
 
• Kuchipudi adheres to the guidelines set in Natya Shastra, blending elements of **bhava** (expression), **raga** (melody), and **tala** (rhythm).
 
 
 
• **Costume and Makeup**
 
 
• Kuchipudi dancers wear **vibrant costumes** similar to Bharatanatyam but with unique draping styles.
 
• Elaborate makeup and jewelry enhance the visual appeal of the performance.
 
 
 
• **Key Elements of Kuchipudi**
 
 
• It involves a combination of **pure dance (nritta)** and **expressive dance (abhinaya)**.
 
• One of the highlights is the **Tarangam**, where dancers perform intricate steps on the edges of a brass plate.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Kuchipudi Performers**
 
 
• Renowned exponents include **Vempati Chinna Satyam** and **Yamini Krishnamurthy**.
 
• They played a pivotal role in popularizing Kuchipudi on global platforms.

questions.question: What is the primary environmental impact of the release of freon from refrigeration plants on the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stratospheric ozone depletion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Freon is a trade name for a group of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which are synthetic compounds primarily used in refrigeration, air conditioning, and aerosol propellants.
 
• When released into the atmosphere, freon compounds rise into the stratosphere, where they are broken down by ultraviolet (UV) radiation, releasing chlorine atoms.
 
• These chlorine atoms react with ozone molecules (O₃) in the stratosphere, causing the depletion of the ozone layer.
 
• Stratospheric ozone depletion reduces the layer that protects Earth from harmful UV-B radiation, leading to increased risks of skin cancer, cataracts, and harm to ecosystems.
 
• The Montreal Protocol, signed in 1987, is an international treaty designed to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances like freon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Layer:**

 
 
• The ozone layer is a region in the Earth's stratosphere that absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.
 
• It is primarily located between 15 and 35 kilometers above Earth's surface.
 
• Depletion of the ozone layer results in the "ozone hole," which is particularly prominent over Antarctica.
 
 
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs):**
 
 
• CFCs are man-made chemical compounds composed of carbon, chlorine, and fluorine.
 
• They were widely used in refrigerants, aerosol propellants, and foam-blowing agents before being regulated.
 
• CFCs have a high atmospheric lifetime and are significant contributors to ozone depletion.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Ozone Depletion:**
 
 
• Increased UV radiation exposure can lead to skin cancers, cataracts, and suppression of the immune system in humans.
 
• It also negatively impacts marine ecosystems, especially phytoplankton, which are the foundation of aquatic food chains.
 
• Excess UV radiation can inhibit plant growth and reduce agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol:**
 
 
• The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer is an international treaty adopted in 1987.
 
• It aims to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances (ODS).
 
• This treaty is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements, contributing to the recovery of the ozone layer.
